record.original_question: Characterize the Banach spaces X for which the vector-valued Lebesgue space L^p([0, 1], X), with 1 < p < ∞, has an unconditional basis.

evidence.quote: Problem 5.4. Characterize those Banach spaces X such that L^p([0, 1], X) has unconditional basis (1 < p < ∞).

artifact.category_tag: unconditional bases in vector-valued Lp spaces
artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $X$ be a (real or complex) infinite-dimensional Banach space, and let $1 < p < \infty$. Let $L^p([0,1], X)$ denote the Bochner space of (equivalence classes of) strongly measurable functions $f : [0,1] \to X$ such that $\|f\|_{L^p(X)} := \left( \int_0^1 \|f(t)\|_X^p \, dt \right)^{1/p} < \infty$, equipped with this norm. A sequence $(e_n)_{n \ge 1}$ in a Banach space $E$ is called a Schauder basis of $E$ if every $x \in E$ admits a unique representation $x = \sum_{n=1}^\infty a_n e_n$ converging in norm; the basis is called unconditional if this series converges unconditionally for every $x \in E$. 

Give a characterization, in terms of intrinsic Banach-space properties of $X$, of those Banach spaces $X$ for which $L^p([0,1], X)$ admits an unconditional Schauder basis.
artifact.status_search_result: No published characterization of those Banach spaces $X$ for which $L^p([0,1],X)$ has an unconditional basis appears in the literature retrieved by web search. Standard references discuss unconditional bases in scalar $L^p$ and the related notion of UMD spaces (which is necessary), but a full characterization for the vector-valued Bochner space $L^p([0,1],X)$ remains apparently open.

status_evidence.title: Unconditional Bases in Banach Spaces (Springer)
status_evidence.snippet: General theory of unconditional bases in Banach spaces; no characterization stated for L^p([0,1],X) with general X.
status_evidence.claim: No characterization for vector-valued L^p is given in standard references on unconditional bases.

status_evidence.title: Uniqueness of unconditional bases in Banach spaces (Kalton et al.)
status_evidence.snippet: Discusses uniqueness up to permutation of unconditional bases in various Banach spaces but does not characterize when L^p([0,1],X) has an unconditional basis.
status_evidence.claim: The characterization problem for unconditional bases of L^p([0,1],X) is not resolved in the cited unconditional-basis literature.
